# Policy-vs-Code Contradictions -- Ranked

Generated 2026-08-01. Scope: `docs/policies/` (46 files) correlated against `ast_call_graph.json`
(2,218 nodes) and direct source reads. 8 of 46 policies are classified CONTRADICTED (policy states X,
code does not-X) out of the full six-status matrix in `policy_enforcement_raw.json`. Ranked by
operational severity: how much of the policy's SHALL is unmet, how often the gap fires, and how
directly it undermines something else in the corpus.

## 1. [SEEDED, RE-VERIFIED] `docs/policies/callgraph-analysis-policy.md`

**Claim:** An AST-based CallGraph (578+ classes, 3,985+ methods, 4 languages) drives impact-analysis
decisions at pre-analysis, implementation and review steps.

**Reality:** `langgraph_engine/parsers/config.py:11` hard-codes `MAX_FILES = 300`. A real (not
simulated) invocation of `call_graph_builder.py` against this repo returned `files_analyzed: 300`
against 411 actual `.py` files. Because the builder's file-discovery order is alphabetical-by-subpackage
within `langgraph_engine/`, its budget is exhausted before reaching `s*`-prefixed packages:
**`langgraph_engine/sdlc_pipeline/` -- the entire Level-2 SDLC execution core, 45/45 files -- is 100%
absent from its output**, along with 38/45 files across the three canonical hook packages
(`pre_tool_enforcer/`, `post_tool_tracker/`, `stop_notifier/`). Meanwhile 75 of the 300-file budget
(25%) is spent on `tests/`, which is not even in the policy's stated live scope.

**Why it's #1:** CLAUDE.md advertises this exact mechanism as "578 classes, 3,985 methods... heavily
ALIVE" and cites it as informing decisions at Steps 0/4/5 (current numbering). Every impact analysis
the pipeline has ever run has been blind to the code it is supposed to be orchestrating. This also
propagates: `test-generation-policy.md`'s third trigger ("CallGraph flags a risk-prioritized untested
gap") inherits the same blindness for the same package.

**Evidence:** `docs/phase-0-reverse-engineering/builder_divergence.md` (full table); `parsers/config.py:11`.

## 2. `docs/policies/session-memory-policy.md`, `session-pruning-policy.md`, `git-auto-commit-policy.md` -- one root cause, three broken SHALLs, firing every turn

**Claim (three separate policies):** the system SHALL persist session summaries locally
(session-memory), SHALL keep the last 10 sessions and archive >30-day-old ones (session-pruning), and
SHALL auto-commit on phase completion / every 3-5 files (git-auto-commit).

**Reality:** `hooks/stop_notifier/core.py` -- which fires on **every AI response turn**, not once per
session (verified against its own docstring at `core.py:44-61`) -- guards each of these three
maintenance subprocess calls with an `if <script>.exists():` check before running:

| Policy | Expected script | Guard line | Exists on disk? |
|---|---|---|---|
| git-auto-commit | `scripts/architecture/03-execution-system/09-git-commit/git-auto-commit-policy.py` | `core.py:78` | **No** |
| session-memory | `scripts/architecture/01-sync-system/session-management/auto-save-session.py` | `core.py:106` | **No** |
| session-pruning | `scripts/architecture/01-sync-system/session-management/archive-old-sessions.py` | `core.py:135` | **No** |
| session-pruning | `scripts/architecture/01-sync-system/session-pruner.py` | `core.py:159` | **No** |

Verified directly against the filesystem (`find scripts/architecture` and targeted `find -iname`
passes): the entire `scripts/architecture/01-sync-system/` subtree and
`scripts/architecture/03-execution-system/09-git-commit/` subtree do not exist. Only
`00-code-graph-analysis/` and `failure-prevention/` exist under `03-execution-system/`. Because every
guard is a silent `.exists()` check (not a try/except around a `FileNotFoundError`), **none of these
four blocks even logs a warning** -- they no-op completely, every single turn, with zero trace in
`stop-notifier.log`.

**Why it's #2:** unlike CallGraph (which only matters when impact analysis is actually consulted),
this fires on every response and silently fails all three SHALLs it's chartered to fulfil, with no
diagnostic signal that anything is wrong.

**Evidence:** `hooks/stop_notifier/core.py:74-181`; `find scripts/architecture` (2 files + 1 pycache +
1 data file, not the ~10+ implied by the referenced paths).

## 3. `docs/policies/architecture-script-mapping-policy.md`

**Claim:** documents which architecture scripts physically exist in `scripts/architecture/` and maps
each to its pipeline step -- i.e. its entire reason for existing is to be an accurate map of the
filesystem.

**Reality:** it is wrong about its own subject in at least four independent ways: (a) its own header
says "Total Architecture Scripts: 3" while its own Summary Statistics table says 6 -- internal
self-contradiction; (b) it lists `standards-loader.py`, `anti-hallucination-enforcement.py` and
`prompt-generator.py` as living in `scripts/architecture/` -- they don't; those names exist only under
the differently-rooted `langgraph_engine/sdlc_pipeline/architecture/`; (c) its "Migration: What
Happened to the Other 59 Scripts" table names 12 target modules
(`session_manager.py`, `checkpoint_manager.py`, `backup_manager.py`, `context_cache.py`,
`context_deduplicator.py`, `token_manager.py`, `version_selector.py`, `git_operations.py`,
`github_facade.py`, `progress_display.py`, `skill_manager.py`, `skill_agent_loader.py`) -- none exist
anywhere in the 335-file live-scope structural inventory; (d) it cites
`langgraph_engine/level3_execution/subgraph.py`, a path CLAUDE.md documents as renamed to
`sdlc_pipeline/` well before this document's stated 2026-03-17 last-update date.

**Why it's #3:** it is the one policy in the corpus whose entire content is a factual claim about the
filesystem, and the filesystem does not agree with it on almost every specific it makes.

**Evidence:** direct `find scripts/architecture` + `find langgraph_engine` cross-checks; see the full
record in `policy_enforcement_raw.json`.

## 4. `docs/policies/anti-hallucination-enforcement.md`

**Claim:** integrated with prompt generation (old Step 0 / current Step 1) to require think-first,
search-before-answer, verify-before-output.

**Reality:** `langgraph_engine/sdlc_pipeline/architecture/00-prompt-generation/anti_hallucination_enforcement.py`
is a well-formed module with `validate()`/`enforce()`/`report()` functions, but it has **zero
importers anywhere in `langgraph_engine/`** (repo-wide grep for `import anti_hallucination` / `from
... anti_hallucination`: no matches). It is CHA-"reachable" only because it has its own `__main__`
CLI entry point, which the AST pass seeds as an entry point regardless of production use -- a known
confound distinct from genuine liveness. The current live Step-1 chain
(`prompt_gen_expert_caller.py` -> `todo_decomposer.py` -> `orchestrator_agent_caller.py`) never calls
it.

**Why it's #4:** a named safety/quality policy with real code behind it that the pipeline simply never
invokes -- a policy that looks ENFORCED under a naive reachability check but is not, on inspection of
who actually imports it.

**Evidence:** `policy_enforcement_raw.json` record for this file; `grep -r "anti_hallucination"` import
search across `langgraph_engine/`.

## 5. `docs/policies/intelligent-decision-engine-policy.md`

**Claim:** a single mandatory OpenRouter LLM call at "Step 3.3A" replaced 4 separate keyword-based
decision systems (task type, complexity, model selection, skill/agent selection), with no keyword
fallback.

**Reality:** no `OpenRouter`/`openrouter` string, no `Step 3.3A`, no dedicated decision-engine module
exists anywhere in live scope. CLAUDE.md's own version history states the opposite trajectory: v1.13
**removed** the separate plan-mode/skill-selection/model-selection steps outright (not merged into one
call), and v1.20 replaced the remaining monolithic orchestrator call with a TODO-decomposition
pipeline. There was never a consolidation into one OpenRouter call to find -- the four systems this
policy claims to have unified were deleted, not merged, so even a topology-aware retranslation finds
no equivalent step.

**Why it's #5:** unlike most of the corpus's staleness (renamed steps, same underlying mechanism), this
policy describes an architecture that was never built as described; it is CONTRADICTED even after
retranslation, not merely STALE-TOPOLOGY.

**Evidence:** zero-match greps across the full 2,218-node index and `langgraph_engine/` source tree for
`OpenRouter`, `decision_engine`, `intelligent_decision`, `Step 3.3A`.

## 6. `docs/policies/tool-usage-optimization-policy.md`

**Claim:** "v2.0.0 CONSOLIDATED... NO DUPLICATION" -- a five-stage (analyze/optimize/validate/execute/
minimize) optimization pipeline at "Step 5" that supersedes prior ADVANCED-TOKEN-OPTIMIZATION.md /
TOKEN-OPTIMIZATION-COMPLETE.md guidance.

**Reality:** there is no separate "Step 5" code path or five-stage pipeline. This policy's only real
enforcement mechanism is the exact same PreToolUse hook checks
(`hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/policies/read_opt.py`, `grep_opt.py`) that `tool-optimization-policy.md`
already claims, and a third file, `docs/standards/TOOL-OPTIMIZATION-LEVEL2-STANDARD.md`, describes the
same subject again. The specific "NO DUPLICATION" claim this policy makes about itself is the exact
opposite of what both Part A (corpus reconciliation) and this pass confirm.

**Why it's #6:** lowest-severity of the eight -- the underlying mechanism does work (see
`tool-optimization-policy.md`, ENFORCED, confirmed by this agent's own tool calls being blocked live
during this task) -- but this document's specific self-description is false.

**Evidence:** shared enforcement point confirmed identical to `tool-optimization-policy.md`'s record in
`policy_enforcement_raw.json`; Part A's `policy_corpus_summary.md` contradiction #2.
